text: Every night, an old guard asked the bank to lock him inside its vault. He took one candle and nothing else. The clerk laughed. They said he was guarding the gold from himself. Only the owner, master Braille, held the key. But the guard insisted. So every evening, Braille turned the key on him. And every morning, he opened it again. And every morning, the gold was untouched. Through the door, they heard him topping all night with his ring. Braille called him mad and cut his pay. The guard thanked him and asked to stay another year. Weeks came months. His candles were shorter. His knees were stiff. Then, one morning, Braille opened the door. The chests were empty. The shelves were empty. The guard was gone and so was every coin. The door had been locked all night. The walls looked perfect. You see, a solid wall sounds dull when you tab it. A hollow one rings. His ring found an old drain behind the stone. From before the bank was built, each night, he chipped away a little. Then filled the hole with candle wax and rubbed it gray with ash. By morning, nobody could tell. On the last night, he crawled through with the gold. For months, the bank had locked in in with the gold and paid him for it.
